chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nasir, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida, from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them). He said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the ascetic in this world.
He said: The one who abandons its lawful things out of fear of being held to account for them, and abandons its unlawful things out of fear of punishment.

key_terms.الزاهد: The ascetic (zahid), one who renounces worldly pleasures
key_terms.حرام: That which is forbidden and prohibited
key_terms.حساب: Reckoning, accountability before God on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.حلال: That which is lawful and permissible in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of an ascetic (zahid) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to define the ascetic (zahid) in this world. He provided a profound definition: the true ascetic avoids not only the haram (forbidden) out of fear of divine punishment, but also avoids the halal (permissible) out of fear of being questioned about it on the Day of Judgment. This teaching, transmitted through a chain of Imams including al-Rida and Musa al-Kadhim, reflects the elevated standard of spiritual discipline in Shia ethics where accountability extends even to permissible enjoyments.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
